subject: Hosted rate card: reconciling token-match across streaming, tools, and invoices
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSCo Billing <billing@saasco.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on Mar invoice — need help reconciling token counts

Hi Mina,

We’re reconciling March invoices and noticed our parsing of model-usage exports doesn’t match the billed token totals on invoice #SA-0317. Two specific questions:

1) When a request includes a system prompt + user prompt + a tool call, how should we attribute tokens to input vs output on your hosted API export? Our parser currently tags tool outputs as "tool" tokens but the invoice line items appear under model-output.

2) For streaming responses: if the client disconnects mid-stream, do you bill the full tokenized output that the model generated, or only the tokens that were successfully streamed/acknowledged to the client? We have a few sessions where the client dropped at token boundary and totals diverge by ~12%.

3) Rounding: are tokens rounded per chunk/stream chunk, per request, or per-invoice line? Our token-export shows fractional counts coming from a tokenizer conversion step.

I attached our token-export.csv and invoice JSON. Can you point us to the exact mapping between your hosted rate card lines and the per-request token breakdown? If helpful, happy to hop on a quick call — this is blocking our AP team.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Revenue Ops, SaaSCo
phone: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: token-export-0317.csv (CSV of parsed model calls), saasco-invoice-0317.json (invoice snapshot)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Mar invoice — need help reconciling token counts

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the exports. High level answers first, then concrete examples below:

- Attribution: we treat system prompts and user prompts sent to the model as input tokens. Tool *inputs* (arguments passed to a tool) are counted as input tokens to the model that executed the tool, and tool *outputs* (what the tool returns and is then included in the model context) are counted as output tokens on that model invocation. In your invoice example it sounds like tool outputs were surfaced under the model-output line item — that is expected when the tool was executed as a model call (e.g., model invoked a parsing tool hosted by Redwood).

- Streaming disconnects: billing is based on actual model invocations and the final generated tokens as committed by the model process. If a client disconnects before the model finishes but the model had already generated tokens that reached our commit buffer, those tokens are billed. We do not bill speculative micro-chunks that were never materialized by the model. Practically: we bill final tokens per model invocation; partial generation that was aborted before the model emitted any token is not billed.

- Rounding: tokens are rounded at the model-invocation level (per-request). We tokenize the input and the final output; we sum input + output for that invocation and then round each of input and output up to the nearest whole token for reporting. We do not round per-stream-chunk. This prevents small fractional differences accumulating across streaming frames.

Concrete example (from your CSV):
- Request A: system 12.7 tokens, user 34.3 tokens, model output 123.6 tokens (streamed in 8 frames). We round to system=13, user=35, output=124; billed as input=48 tokens, output=124 tokens for that invocation.

- Tool call example: main model invoked tool T (tool input 8.2 tokens). Tool executes a separate model invocation returning 22.9 tokens. That 22.9 is billed as output on the tool invocation; if the main model then includes the tool output in its context, the bytes re-tokenized and counted as input to the next main-model invocation per the logs.

Action items: I’m attaching the Redwood rate card (PDF) and a short reconciliation guide. Marissa / Ben — please review the CSV Alice attached and confirm the two suspect request IDs: 001234 and 001237. If there’s an exporter mismatch we can run a reconciliation job and provide a line-level audit.

Would you like a short call Mon or Tue? If AP needs a formal credit request we can start the review immediately.

—
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasco.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 19:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Mar invoice — need help reconciling token counts

Adding a technical example to avoid ambiguity in the reconciliation job:

- We tokenize with the same tokenizer version used for billing (v3.1) — the exporter should use that same tokenizer to match counts. If you used a different tokenizer or post-processed the token CSV (e.g., converting bytes back to tokens with a different library) you'll see fractional differences.

- Rounding rule is implemented as: round_up(floor_tokens + fractional_tokens) applied per field (system/user/output) per invocation. That means small fractions like 0.2+0.3 across two fields will be rounded independently, which can look like extra tokens compared to a single-pass global rounding.

Example math we’ll use in the reconciliation job:
Main invocation: system 5.6 -> 6, user 14.4 -> 15, output 201.1 -> 202
Tool invocation (secondary): input 9.7 -> 10, tool output 37.8 -> 38
If the main invocation later ingests the tool output as context, the re-tokenization will show those 38 tokens as input on the follow-up invocation and billed accordingly.

I’ll run a diff between your token-export-0317.csv and our raw call logs overnight and share a line-level mapping for the two RIDs Mina called out.

—Ben
Principal Engineer, Billing Systems

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Mar invoice — need help reconciling token counts

Thanks Mina and Ben — that helps a lot. Couple of follow-ups after scanning the example mapping you provided:

- We have ~120 sessions where the client explicitly closed the socket after receiving the last frame; in your policy wording above it sounds like those should not be billed unless the model had committed tokens. Our logs show the model claimed to have generated the final token but the gateway didn't ack the frame back to the client. Can you confirm whether the gateway ack status or the model commit is the ground truth for billing?

- If there is a >10% variance between our exported totals and the invoice after your reconciliation, what is Redwood's standard credit policy? Our AP team will escalate unless we have a clear remediation path.

We can provide a list of the 120 session ids if that helps with the audit. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alice

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Mar invoice — need help reconciling token counts

Alice — quick answers and next steps:

- Billing ground truth: model commit. The gateway ack is best-effort for delivery; billing is tied to the model process that emitted and committed the tokens. In the narrow cases you described where the gateway failed to ack but the model commit occurred, those tokens are counted. If the model aborted before emitting/committing the token there is nothing to bill.

- Credit policy: standard practice is to run the reconciliation within 30 days of invoice issuance. If, after the audit, the reconciled billed amount deviates >10% in Redwood’s favor (meaning we overcharged relative to our audit), we issue a credit for the difference on the following invoice. For larger disputes or repeated discrepancies we escalate to a formal credit review with finance.

Next steps from our side:
1) Ben will upload a line-level mapping CSV to the shared Drive by EOD today (mapping our invocation IDs to your CSV rows).
2) If you can share the 120 session IDs we’ll prioritize those and provide a short report showing for each session: (a) model invocation id, (b) tokenizer counts pre-rounding, (c) rounding delta, (d) whether token was committed.
3) If the review shows >10% net overcharge we’ll issue a credit and copy AP on the credit memo.

I’m attaching a short "token-reconciliation-guidance.md" stub that explains how to export compatible token counts and the tokenizer version to use for parity. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute reconciliation call with Ben and Marissa this week.

Thanks for flagging this — we’ll get it resolved quickly.

—
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
